verdicts.title: No fused-vs-unfused parity test exists for the generic QKV wrapper on any device; the Gemma3 device-independent pipeline pattern was not reused for Qwen3 or the generic path
verdicts.reasoning: Verified every structural link in the current tree. (1) grep over packages/ shows _make_fused_qkv_attention_forward and _fused_qkv_qwen3_attention_forward are referenced ONLY in src (packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/peft/components/qkv.py:45,87 and components/qkv_qwen3.py:22,90,116) and by no test file; _resolve_fused_qkv_forward_factory appears in exactly one test (tests/peft/test_gemma3_fused_lora_qkv.py:10,70). (2) tests/peft/test_fused_lora_qkv.py:26-51 is the only non-CUDA test and asserts only hasattr(attn,'_opaque_fused_qkv') plus torch.isfinite(logits); line 54 '@pytest.mark.cuda class TestFusedLoRAQKV' gates every numeric test, as claimed. (3) tests/peft/test_glm4_lora.py:21 has a module-level CUDA skipif and :43 an additional @pytest.mark.cuda; tests/peft/test_fused_lora_parallel_residual.py:19/25 likewise, and its Cohere2 tests use num_hidden_layers=1 and compare vmap-vs-eager of the SAME fused model (lines 29,114), so they cannot detect wrapper-vs-upstream divergence. (4) The Gemma3 device-independent pattern exists exactly as described (tests/peft/test_gemma3_fused_lora_qkv.py:126-139 _install_reference_fused_qkv, class TestGemma3FusedWrapperPipeline at :143 with four allclose-vs-upstream tests at :146,165,185,216) and is not reused anywhere else. (5) The consequence is real: I diffed the generic wrapper (qkv.py:155-164) against upstream transformers 5.15.1 and it omits sliding_window for MistralAttention/Cohere2Attention/Qwen2Attention/Gemma2Attention and softcap for Gemma2Attention; instantiating tiny configs gives Gemma2 sliding_window=4096 and attn_logit_softcapping=50.0, Mistral 4096, Cohere2 layer-0 4096, while Qwen2 (use_sliding_window=False) yields None and Glm4Attention never passes it -- i.e. the two CUDA families that DO exercise the generic wrapper are precisely the two where omitting the kwarg is a no-op. CORRECTION: the title's 'on any device' is overstated. tests/peft/test_glm4_lora.py:211 test_glm4_qkv_fusion_matches_unfused_forward IS a genuine fused-vs-unfused logits parity test routed through the generic wrapper (CUDA-only), and the wrapper's own 'if not hidden_states.is_cuda: return original_forward(...)' bail-out (qkv.py:110) means a naive CPU parity test would pass vacuously -- which is why the Gemma3 pattern calls the inner forward directly. Severity lowered from medium to low: this is a test-gap meta-finding requiring only new tests; the concrete numerical harm belongs to the separately reported wrapper defects and should not be counted twice. Not a duplicate of open #880 (restoring CUDA markers on existing kernel tests) or #968 (packing projections into fewer GEMMs).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: The generic QKV wrapper _make_fused_qkv_attention_forward serves eight families (Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Gemma2, Granite, Cohere2, Qwen2, Glm4) and is named by no test. Its only end-to-end parity coverage is CUDA-only and uses Glm4 (test_glm4_lora.py:211) and Qwen2 -- the two families for which the wrapper's omission of upstream's sliding_window/softcap kwargs is a no-op (Qwen2 use_sliding_window=False -> None; Glm4 never passes it). No test, on any device, compares the wrapper against upstream attention for Gemma2 (sliding_window=4096, attn_logit_softcapping=50.0), Mistral (4096) or Cohere2 (4096), so the dropped-kwarg divergence in those families is invisible to CI, and any new entry added to _FUSEABLE_QKV_ATTENTION_CLASSES ships with no parity check. The Gemma3 device-independent pipeline suite (_install_reference_fused_qkv + allclose against attn(...) on CPU) is the working pattern that would catch this and was not reused for the generic path or for Qwen3.

verdicts.title: _auto_fuse_lora skips MLP fusion for any layer whose attention is already QKV-patched
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/peft/peft/_router.py is at packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/peft/_router.py; lines 67-72 read 'attn = getattr(layer, "self_attn", None)' / 'if attn is not None:' / 'if getattr(attn, "_opaque_lora_qkv_patched", False):' / 'continue', and the MLP-fusion half of the same 'for layer in layers:' body starts at line 99, so the guard skips the whole remaining iteration. Within one call this is harmless (the flag is set at the END of the QKV block), so it only bites on a second call. I built a tiny 2-layer Llama + PEFT LoRA and ran three cases with the repo venv: (A) single call with LoRA on q/k/v/gate/up/down -> qkv fused True, mlp fused True; (B) same model with _opaque_lora_qkv_patched pre-set on each attn -> mlp fused False and 'forward' not in vars(mlp); (C) fully realistic two-call flow -- first apply_peft_model_patches with LoRA on q/k/v only (qkv fused, mlp not eligible), then model.add_adapter('mlpad', targets gate/up/down), then apply_peft_model_patches again -> mlp fused False even though gate_proj now has lora_A. Counterfactual isolating the cause: deleting ONLY the _opaque_lora_qkv_patched attribute before the second call in case C makes mlp fused True. So the 'continue' is the sole cause. There is no model-level early-return that would make this unreachable: apply_peft_model_patches (line 151) only returns early when lora is falsy or _lora_patching_allowed() is False, and it always calls _auto_fuse_lora(model) (line 191). Severity confirmed low: correctness of results is unaffected (the unfused PEFT path is the reference implementation), the loss is throughput only, it needs a second patch call after MLP adapters become eligible, and nothing in the shipped trainer flow does that today (DPTrainer calls apply_model_patches once, _dp_trainer.py:844). Not a duplicate of open #968, which is about packing more projections per GEMM, not about this idempotency guard.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Performance-only, requires two patch calls. On any second call to apply_peft_model_patches for a model whose attention was already QKV-fused, the outer-loop 'continue' at _router.py:72 skips the MLP block at :99-137 for that layer. Reproduced: LoRA on q/k/v only -> apply_peft_model_patches (QKV fused) -> model.add_adapter with gate/up/down targets -> apply_peft_model_patches again leaves every MLP unfused (mlp._opaque_lora_mlp_patched absent, mlp.forward not overridden), while clearing only the _opaque_lora_qkv_patched flag makes the same call fuse them. Numerical results stay correct because the unfused PEFT path is used; the fused-MLP speedup is silently absent with no log line (the logger.debug at :145 only fires when a count is nonzero). No shipped Opaque flow calls the patcher twice today, so this is latent.

verdicts.title: poisson() now accepts whole-horizon and composed processes as its base, silently accounting a mechanism no Opaque sampler realizes
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified, numbers reproduced bit-for-bit with the checked-in extension (packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/opaque_accounting.abi3.so, which exports poisson_pld and no poisson_gaussian_pld, i.e. a post-#850 build). Current tree: _poisson.py:22 '_Inner = DpProcess'; :40-46 the only inner-type check on the plain path is 'if not isinstance(self.inner, DpProcess)'; :161-172 the plain path unconditionally calls _native.poisson_pld(self.inner.pld(...), self.sample_rate) for every inner type; :185-186 the factory docstring still says 'Returns a single-step process - compose externally with ``* num_steps`` for full-training privacy'; the truncated path by contrast still enforces Gaussian/AdaClip/NonPrivate at :91-99. docs/reference/accounting.md:232 and docs/user-guide/accounting.md:114 both state 'Plain Poisson accepts any Opaque DpProcess as its base mechanism' with no per-step caveat. Regression confirmed: 'git show 3b22a6af^:.../_poisson.py' ends with 'match inner: case Gaussian() | AdaClip() | NonPrivate(): pass; case _: raise TypeError("poisson() requires a Gaussian, AdaClip, or NonPrivate inner mechanism, got ...")', and 3b22a6af ('feat(accounting): generalize Poisson PLD amplification (#850)') replaced that with the DpProcess check while adding tests that only exercise a generic PER-STEP base (acc.eps_delta). Measured at HEAD with the repo venv, all values matching the finding exactly: poisson(k_out_of_t(gaussian(1.0), k=2, t=100, allocation='block'), 0.01).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.009738873655638745; the same horizon unamplified = 1.233938641105668 (127x higher); the closest realizable per-step reading poisson(gaussian(1.0),0.01)*100 = 0.7180658390624926 (74x higher); and k_out_of_t(...)*2 = 1.639800931306253 also succeeds, so neither side of the step/horizon boundary is guarded. The library does have the concept: opaque/api/accounting/core/_horizon.py documents DpHorizonProcess as 'A complete fixed-horizon process that cannot be accounted by prefixes' and docs/reference/accounting.md:283 types k_out_of_t as returning DpHorizonProcess -- the marker exists and Poisson.__post_init__ simply does not consult it. Severity kept at medium, not raised: the returned number is a mathematically valid bound for a different mechanism (one dataset-level Bernoulli(q) coin, then the whole horizon on survivors), no shipped Opaque sampler realizes that model, and no Opaque source path, factory, calibration helper or documented example nests a horizon or composed process inside poisson() -- I grepped every poisson( call site in packages/*/src and docs and all pass gaussian/adaclip. Reaching the understated number requires the user to write the nested call themselves, which the 'accepts any DpProcess' docs invite but the 'single-step' contract in the same docstring contradicts. Not critical (not reachable at defaults) and not low (a documented public API silently returns a 127x-understated epsilon with no warning where it previously raised TypeError).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user writes dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.k_out_of_t(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.0), k=2, t=100, allocation='block'), 0.01) -- accepted at HEAD, returns epsilon_at(1e-5)=0.0097389 for the whole 100-step run. The same horizon accounted correctly (k_out_of_t alone, which is what KOutOfTSampler actually realizes, since it has no dataset-level inclusion coin) is 1.2339386, i.e. 127x higher; the closest realizable per-step reading, poisson(gaussian(1.0),0.01)*100, is 0.7180658. Before #850 the same call raised TypeError. Nothing in Poisson.__post_init__ or Poisson.pld distinguishes a per-step base from a DpHorizonProcess subclass (KOutOfT, CyclicPoisson, BallsInBins, BMinSep) or from a Repeated/Composed spine, and docs/reference/accounting.md:232 plus docs/user-guide/accounting.md:114 advertise 'any Opaque DpProcess' with no caveat. Reachable only by the user writing the nested composition -- no Opaque factory, trainer path, calibration helper or documented example does so -- and the per-step factory docstring (_poisson.py:185) still says to compose externally, so the misuse contradicts one sentence while following another. Unverified: no numerical claim about what mechanism, if any, the returned bound would be correct for beyond the single dataset-level-coin reading, which I reasoned about but did not independently prove against the Feldman-Shenfeld subsampling theorem cited in poisson.rs:17-20.

verdicts.title: Generic Poisson transform costs tightness against the external oracle, and the cross-validation tolerances were relaxed to absorb it
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced the accuracy claim exactly and verified every file citation. Test file (current tree): test_cross_validation.py:47-54 'ATOL = 1e-6', 'POISSON_EPSILON_ATOL = 6e-5', 'POISSON_DELTA_ATOL = 3e-8', 'POISSON_ADVANTAGE_ATOL = 1.3e-5', 'POISSON_BETA_ATOL = 2.2e-4'; :56-58 the stale 'NOTE: opaque and dp_accounting agree to ~1e-9 relative error'; :265-267 'expected = _POISSON_EPSILON_GOLDENS[...]' asserted at ATOL with the oracle asserted at POISSON_EPSILON_ATOL; :343-346 same pattern for epsilon and advantage; :389 beta asserted against riskcal at POISSON_BETA_ATOL. The diff of 3b22a6af confirms the retarget: before it, the oracle comparisons themselves were 'assert ours == pytest.approx(ref, abs=ATOL)' with ATOL=1e-6 and there were no goldens at all; the commit introduced _POISSON_EPSILON/DELTA/ADVANTAGE/BETA_GOLDENS (self-generated -- e.g. (0.5,0.001,1000): 3.2389339479391825) and moved the 1e-6 assertion onto them. Rust structure verified: poisson.rs:24 poisson_pld dispatches a Gaussian-tagged base to :45 poisson_from_gaussian, which rebuilds a disc_dist Gaussian PMF (:65-70), wraps it in new_symmetric so the Gaussian tag is gone, and recurses into the generic pointwise transform; project_transformed_atoms (:233) takes a 'refinement' parameter that both call sites (:337,:352) pass as 1; the analytic poisson_gaussian_epsilon_bounds (:399) and poisson_gaussian_get_delta (:486) survive but are now used only by truncated_poisson.rs (:9,135-153,176-205) and by poisson.rs's own #[test]s (:1033-1096); truncated_poisson.rs:57-61 confirms the truncated path falls back to poisson_pld only when p_trunc == 0.0. Magnitude: I re-ran the test's own 34-point golden grid against dp_accounting (pld_lib.from_gaussian_mechanism(sigma, sampling_prob=q).self_compose(steps).get_epsilon_for_delta(1e-5)) with the checked-in HEAD extension. Worst |ours - dp_accounting| = 5.332389186e-05 at sigma=0.5,q=0.001,steps=1000 (ours 3.2389339498917304 vs google 3.238880625999869) -- identical to the finding's figure -- and every one of the 34 signed differences is positive (minimum +3.37e-08), i.e. always conservative. CORRECTION to the finding's 'four orders of magnitude': I could not measure the pre-#850 analytic path, because the checked-in .so is a post-#850 build that no longer exports poisson_gaussian_pld (contrary to the finding's evidence line), and I did not build the old crate. What IS established is a lower bound on the regression: the pre-#850 suite asserted opaque == dp_accounting to abs=1e-6 on this same grid and was green, so agreement went from <=1e-6 to 5.3e-5, i.e. at least ~53x looser; the specific 3.98e-9 'old' figure and the wider 108-point sweep remain unverified. I also could not isolate the analytic path's accuracy through the truncated API (a large batch cap hits the p_trunc==0.0 fallback and returns the identical generic value; a cap small enough to take the analytic branch changes the mechanism itself, +4.7e-2). Severity lowered from the finding's own low? No -- kept low, and that is the right level: the error is strictly conservative (worst 5.3e-5 absolute, 1.6e-5 relative, epsilon over- not under-stated), so no privacy guarantee is weakened; the residual issues are a utility/tightness regression and test integrity (the only 1e-6 check is now against opaque's own committed numbers, and the 'agree to ~1e-9' note at :56-58 contradicts the tolerances two lines above it, though the relaxation itself is honestly explained at :47-49).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Routing the Poisson-subsampled Gaussian through the generic pointwise transform (poisson.rs:24 -> :45 poisson_from_gaussian -> disc_dist -> project_transformed_atoms with refinement=1) instead of the analytic subsampled-Gaussian curve costs tightness against Google dp_accounting 0.6.0. Measured at HEAD on the test suite's own 34-point grid: worst |opaque - dp_accounting| in epsilon_at(1e-5) = 5.33e-05 (sigma=0.5, q=1e-3, 1000 steps: 3.2389339 vs 3.2388806), with all 34 differences positive (min +3.4e-08), so the bound is always conservative -- epsilon is over-stated, never under-stated, and no privacy claim is weakened. The same commit (3b22a6af, #850) loosened the external-oracle assertions from abs=1e-6 to 6e-5 (epsilon), 1.3e-5 (advantage), 2.2e-4 (beta), 3e-8 (delta) and moved the surviving 1e-6 check onto goldens generated from opaque's own output, so a future change that loses another 6e-5 of epsilon against dp_accounting would pass cross-validation as long as the goldens are regenerated; the module note at test_cross_validation.py:56-58 still claims ~1e-9 agreement. The truncated-Poisson sibling still uses the analytic curve (truncated_poisson.rs:57-61 falls back to poisson_pld only at p_trunc==0.0), so the two Poisson paths no longer share an accuracy characteristic. Unverified: the pre-#850 analytic path's exact agreement with the oracle (claimed 3.98e-9) -- the checked-in extension is a post-#850 build with no poisson_gaussian_pld export, so only 'at least ~53x looser than the previously enforced 1e-6' is established.
